title: AuditRecord
description: One complete audit record per case, written after Stage 2 completes. This is the compliance-facing artifact (BRD §5, §10.3: 13-month retention for Ofcom audit readiness) — treat schema changes here as requiring compliance sign-off, not just an engineering review, since this is literally what you'd hand a regulator to defend an autonomous credit decision.

correlation_id.description: Assigned by the middleware interceptor (BRD US-01) at the moment the case enters the pipeline. Must thread through every log line, every tool call, and any human-review UI referencing this case — this is the join key for reconstructing a case's full history end to end.

customer_id.description: Internal ID only. PII masking (US-02) must have already happened before this record is written — this schema has no field for name/address/etc. by design.

stage1.description: Full record of what Stage 1 decided and why — required even after Stage 1 becomes a real LLM call. If you swap in a real model, capture its actual reasoning trace here, not a paraphrase.

reasoning.description: Human-readable reasoning trace. Rule-based in the POC; should be the model's actual chain-of-reasoning output (or a structured summary of it) once Stage 1 is a real LLM call.

sources_queried.description: What was ACTUALLY fetched — should always equal stage1.sources_selected. Kept as a separate field deliberately: if these two ever diverge in production, that's a bug worth being able to detect from the log alone.

root_cause_type.description: Structured root-cause category. Keep this as a controlled vocabulary (not free text) so KPI dashboards (BRD §12, e.g. 'diagnostic accuracy') can aggregate over it reliably.

explanation.description: Plain-language explanation. This is also what BRD US-13 requires be shown to the customer for any automated resolution — the internal audit log and the customer-facing explanation should be the same text, not two separately-maintained copies that can drift apart.

action.description: MUST come from the Resolution Decision Matrix, enforced in code (see agent.py::_decide_action). An LLM should never be able to write an arbitrary string into this field. POLICY: no monetary adjustment executes without human approval — 'Pending Approval — Credit' and 'Pending Approval — Bill Correction' are proposals awaiting an agent's approval, not completed actions. Only Proactive Notice (informational, no money moves) is ever automatic.

final_action.description: Denormalized copy of stage2.action for fast querying/dashboarding without unpacking the nested object.

human_override.description: NOT YET IN THE POC — required for production per BRD §11.3: 'Human override available on every auto-executed action, logged with agent ID and reason.' Add before Sprint 4.
